name: cmd-d-pins-and-unpins-a-tab
description: Cmd+D on the shown regular tab moves its row into the pinned section, and Cmd+D again returns it to the regular list. The reading is the sidebar DOM - the row counts under the pinned dropzone and under the tabs dropzone - and the window's own log names each move. The fixture starts with two regular rows and nothing pinned, so both counts change in a direction only the toggle can produce.

actions.expression: (() => { const n = s => document.querySelectorAll(s).length; return 'pinned=' + n('[data-dropzone="pinned"] .row.tabrow') + ' tabs=' + n('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .row.tabrow'); })()
actions.note: THE CONTROL: nothing is pinned yet, so a later pinned row cannot be one the fixture already had.

actions.expression: (() => { const n = s => document.querySelectorAll(s).length; return 'pinned=' + n('[data-dropzone="pinned"] .row.tabrow') + ' tabs=' + n('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .row.tabrow'); })()
actions.note: The shown row left the regular list for the pinned one. Both counts move, so a redraw that dropped a row reads differently from a pin.

actions.expression: (() => { const n = s => document.querySelectorAll(s).length; return 'pinned=' + n('[data-dropzone="pinned"] .row.tabrow') + ' tabs=' + n('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .row.tabrow'); })()
actions.note: The same key on the now-pinned row sends it back.

assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the space started with nothing pinned.

assertions.label: the-chord-reached-the-map
assertions.desc: Cmd+D ran the Atrium action rather than Bookmark This Tab.

assertions.label: the-window-pinned-it
assertions.desc: The core moved the row into the pinned list.
The sidebar draws the tab in its pinned section.

assertions.label: the-window-unpinned-it
assertions.desc: The second press moved the row back.
The sidebar draws the tab in its regular list again.
